Quick reconcile on the two valuation framings I posted earlier - Maya / Theo to make sure we're not running both chains as if they were the same answer. Two different chains in play here. (1) The standards section 1.1 sequential method anchored on Cal-Maine (cohort-median public comp at ~10-11x mid-cycle, then scale haircut 35-45%, then private discount 20-25%, then colony-risk haircut tied to Aurora's ~40% colony exposure) is the analytically defensible chain for Aurora specifically - that's the one that lands at 5.0-6.5x FY24 EBITDA and that's where the deck should anchor and where we defend value to IC. The worked example inside standards 1.1 itself uses different illustrative inputs to demonstrate the method, so don't read the example's output as Aurora's number - start with Cal-Maine + Aurora's specific colony exposure and the chain produces 5.0-6.5x. (2) The 8-10x range I mentioned in the earlier reminder is the broker-asking-side haircut framing - start from the 12-14x broker ask, take off ~2x for private/scale, take off ~2x for colony risk, land at 8-10x. That's the asking-side talking point Tasman Mercantile will push back at us with in negotiation; it's not where we defend value to IC. The internal scanned brief also carries an 8-10x reference but that's the same framing (pre the standards-1.1 chain). The deck should anchor on the (1) chain landing at 5.0-6.5x as the working analytical case; the 8-10x is context for the negotiation gap, not the central case. Likewise if anyone in the team reads the standards worked example and lands at ~4.1-4.6x - that's the example's illustrative inputs, not Aurora's. Anchor: 5.0-6.5x.
